title: roadmap-signal-matrix-apr-2026
body:
Purpose
This is a working synthesis of customer feedback (Jan–Mar 2026) focused on actionable product signals for the Q2 roadmap. It aggregates CS cases, renewal conversations, and proactive outreach calls. The goal: surface clusters of requests, estimate relative impact and effort, and propose immediate next steps for Product and Eng to triage.

Methodology & data sources
- Input: 184 CS tickets (tagged 'product-request'), 27 customer interviews (renewals + expansion), 112 Slack mentions in #cs-asks, and 6 partner integration post-mortems.
- Preprocessing: deduped similar asks, clustered by semantic phrases, mapped to product areas (hosted-api, dedicated, private, console, optimize).
- Signal scoring: frequency (how many customers), strategic weight (is it an enterprise blocker?), and urgency (churn risk / sales blocker).

High-level takeaways (executive summary)
1) Strong, recurring theme: predictable quota/throughput controls for Dedicated customers — showing up in renewal talks as a gating item for expansion.
2) Observability gaps: teams want per-request token-cost attribution (not just per-route) and automatic anomaly alerts tied to a prompt set.
3) Private deployments: simplified network onboarding and a 'health-check' suite are frequent asks for regulated customers prepping for pilot.
4) Optimize toolkit requests: customers want prescriptive quantization + rollout recipes (e.g., 'how to quantize and measure regen drop reliably').
5) Low-latency/edge routing: platform teams want clearer SLO routing controls (geo + cost vs latency), with simulated traffic tests.

Signal clusters (descriptions + why it matters)
- Dedicated throughput controls (strength: high; segment: enterprise/dedicated customers): multiple customers reported unexpected throttling during batch ingestion jobs; they request explicit per-tenant throughput buckets and clear billing visibility for bursts.
- Per-request token attribution (strength: medium-high; segment: startups + platform teams): dev teams building cost dashboards want token-level line items in traces to correlate feature usage to costs.
- Private onboarding automation (strength: medium; segment: regulated enterprise): long setup cycles (2–8 weeks) due to networking checklist; ask for CLI-driven preflight and a small test harness.
- Quantization rollout playbooks (strength: medium; segment: applied-ml): requests to standardize A/B testing for quantized models and templates for regressions tests.
- Routing policy simulator (strength: low-medium; segment: platform): ask for ability to simulate traffic mix and show expected latency/cost tradeoffs before applying policies.

Sample customer quotes (verbatim/near-verbatim)
- "We had a sudden backlog during ETL and our Dedicated pool started dropping requests — we can't tolerate this during billing spikes." (Large fintech, renewal call)
- "We spend hours tracing runaway token usage; seeing token cost next to each trace would be a game-changer." (Mid-market product team)
- "Private deployment took four weeks; if there was a checklist we could run ourselves we'd be able to pilot faster." (Healthcare customer)

Priority breakdown (recommendation)
- Immediate (Q2 sprint target): Dedicated throughput controls + clearer burst billing docs; Per-request token attribution (MVP: add token cost column to existing traces).
- Short term (Q2–Q3): Private onboarding automation (CLI preflight + health-check); Observability alerts for prompt set regressions (tie to Optimize).
- Mid term (Q3–Q4): Quantization rollout playbooks + integration with CI; Routing policy simulator.

Impact and rough effort estimates (triangle estimates)
- Dedicated throughput controls: impact = high; effort = medium-high (infra + billing + console).
- Token-level attribution in traces: impact = medium-high; effort = low-medium (tracing instrumentation + UI column).
- Private onboarding automation: impact = medium; effort = medium (scripts + packaging + docs).
- Quantization playbook: impact = medium; effort = medium (content + small tooling).
- Routing simulator: impact = low-medium; effort = medium-high (simulator + UX).

Segmentation notes (who cares most)
- Enterprise/Dedicated: throughput/bursting, SLA clarity, private onboarding.
- Platform/internal infra teams: routing controls, simulators, token attribution.
- Applied-ML / Research teams: quantization playbooks and CI integration.
- Startups/SMB: simpler cost visibility and default-safe routing (lower complexity).

Open questions & risks
- Do we have telemetry coverage across Dedicated nodes to reliably surface per-tenant burst metrics? (Eng action item)
- Will token-level attribution significantly increase trace payloads and storage costs for heavy customers? (SRE / Observability to weigh in)
- For private onboarding automation, what is the minimum viable 'test harness' that satisfies compliance teams? (Security & Legal consult)

Proposed immediate actions (owner recommendations)
- CS: compile top-10 customers most impacted by Dedicated throttling and open customer-specific playbooks (owner: Asha).
- Eng/Platform: spike (2w) to validate telemetry coverage for per-tenant throughput and estimate storage delta for token-attribution traces (owner: Daniel Kwan).
- Product: draft a one-pager spec for 'Dedicated throughput controls' and map required console changes (owner: Liam O'Neill).
- Docs/DevRel: prepare a private-deployment quickstart + CLI preflight checklist (owner: Sofia Martinez).

Next steps (near-term timeline)
- Week 1: CS sends top-10 impacted customer list and schedules 30-min follow-ups to confirm acceptance criteria (Asha).
- Week 2: Eng spike complete and findings shared in Eng sync (Daniel).
- Week 3: Product one-pager reviewed and prioritized at PM sync; decide if we allocate a Q2 ticket.
- Week 4: Draft MVP implementations for token-level attribution and a console column shipped as an experimental flag.

Appendix: short glossary and ticket seeds
- "Burst bucket": per-customer reserved throughput pool for Dedicated nodes.
- "Token attribution": association of generated tokens to request IDs in trace logs for cost analysis.
- Suggested seed tickets: CSREQ-412 (Dedicated bursts), OBS-789 (token attribution trace column), PRIV-60 (private CLI preflight).

Notes on tone and usage
This is a working synthesis intended for Product + Eng prioritization discussion. It contains customer-forward phrasing (quotes anonymized where requested). Use this doc to align on tradeoffs and to seed the first round of implementation tickets.

Contact for clarifications
Asha Raman (customer-success) — asha.raman@redwood.ai
